fields.v: Hu, H., Zhang, Q., Yu, S., Chen, Z., Luo, T., Fang, C., Chen, Z., Xiao, L. (2026). Beyond the Model: Demystifying Harness Effects in Software Engineering Agents. arXiv:2609.32459v1 [cs.SE], 26 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv (cs.SE), page header 'ISE Research'; venue Not stated
Nanjing University of Science and Technology, China (Hu, Q. Zhang, Zhifei Chen, Xiao); Technical University of Munich, Germany (Yu); Nanjing University, China (Luo, Fang, Zhenyu Chen)

Compares; secondary: Proposes an approach — Study 1: two harnesses (mini-SWE-agent, OpenCode) x 10 open-weight models x 3 benchmarks (60 configurations); Study 2: component-level ablation with NanoHarness, the authors' modular harness built on mini-SWE-agent (tool registry, context compression, explicit planning, subagents, lazy skills), compared with OpenCode and Claude Code
fields.why: NanoHarness is listed as contribution (2) but is built mainly as an ablation vehicle for the empirical study; 'Compares' with secondary 'Proposes an approach' is defensible, 'Evaluates' with no secondary is also possible and would remove Q13
fields.doubt: O NanoHarness é contribuição declarada mas serve sobretudo para a ablação; decide se a natureza secundária 'Proposes an approach' se mantém (afeta a aplicação de Q13).

fields.v: Agent harnesses: mini-SWE-agent (lightweight, bash-only), OpenCode (product-level), Claude Code (Table 6 only); no versions stated. NanoHarness (authors', no version) with five plug-in components: tool registry (read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob), context compression, explicit planning (TodoWrite-style todo_write), general SE subagents / task-specific subagents, lazy skills (SKILL.md). Secondary data: matched-model SWE-bench Verified leaderboard results (SWE-agent, OpenHands, Tools)

N/A (no specification artefacts). NanoHarness components use: a todo list (max 10 items, one in_progress) rendered into the prompt; SKILL.md files with metadata forming a skill catalog (6 skills: Terminal Workflow, Minimal Implementation, Build Diagnostics, Test Triage, CLI Fuzzing, Submission Review, Table 1); structured subagent reports via finish_subagent

Not stated as a development flow (agent loop). NanoHarness general subagents follow the SDLC: requirement_analysis, architecture_design, code_generation, test_generation, defect_repair; task-specific subagents: behaviour analysis, differential testing, submission review; parent agent keeps task control, budget and final submission
None (autonomous benchmark runs)
Full harnesses run on benchmarks (Study 1); each NanoHarness component added individually and all combined (ablation, Study 2)

Both: existing code bases (SWE-bench Pro issue repair; GitTaskBench repository-centric task solving) and new project (ProgramBench repository generation from scratch)

No success criterion stated by the authors for any configuration; values only. Study 1 (temperature 0.0, non-thinking mode; per-model values mostly only in Figures 5-10; endpoint values given): (a) mini-SWE-agent + Qwen3.7-Max: SWE-bench Pro 37.3%; (b) OpenCode + Qwen3.7-Max: SWE-bench Pro 40.0% (gap 2.67 pp; gap for Qwen3-Max about 6 pp); (c) mini-SWE-agent + DeepSeek-V4-Pro: SWE-bench Pro 33.7%; (d) OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 34.3%. ProgramBench N=70 endpoint labels 52.3/47.8 (Qwen3.7-Max) and 48.2/41.7 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro); GitTaskBench 74.1/72.2 (Qwen3.7-Max) and 72.2/70.4 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro); the figure labels do not say which harness each value belongs to, but the RQ1.2 text (complex harnesses benefit the strongest models on ProgramBench and GitTaskBench) implies the higher value is OpenCode (ProgramBench 52.3 and 48.2; GitTaskBench 74.1 and 72.2) and the lower mini-SWE-agent. Other 8 models x 2 harnesses x 3 benchmarks: figures only. Study 2, ProgramBench N=200 (ablation): (e) mini-SWE-agent + Qwen3.7-Max: 42.88, 104.13 steps, 3,978,148 prompt tokens/sample; (f) +tools: +4.57 pp; (g) +planning and (h) +skills: +1.36/+0.81 pp (order from figure); (i) +context compression: -4.86 pp, prompt tokens -54.29%; (j) +task-specific subagents: +5.91 pp; (k) +general subagents: -0.70 pp; (l) NanoHarness (all): 50.25 (+7.37 pp), prompt tokens +16.37%, tool calls +131.18%. (m) mini-SWE-agent + DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 45.14, 10,065,204 prompt tokens; (n) +tools +3.54; (o) +planning +0.77; (p) +skills +3.07 (figure order); (q) +context -3.85, prompt tokens -77.02%; (r) +specific subagents +4.46; (s) +general subagents -2.31; (t) NanoHarness: 51.35 (+6.21), prompt tokens +7.26%. Product harnesses on ProgramBench: (u) OpenCode + Qwen3.7-Max 51.68, (v) Claude Code + Qwen3.7-Max 52.33, (w) OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Pro 52.48, (x) Claude Code + DeepSeek-V4-Pro 52.76. fields.v: Tasks: three public benchmarks (random subsets in RQ1, same instances across matched configurations). Configurations: Study 1 3 benchmarks x 2 harnesses x 10 models (Qwen3-Max, Qwen3.5-Plus, Qwen3.6-Plus, Qwen3.6-Max, Qwen3.7-Max; DeepSeek-R1, -V3 (0324), -V3.1, -V3.2, -V4-Pro); Study 2 mini-SWE-agent + each component, NanoHarness, OpenCode, Claude Code, with Qwen3.7-Max and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Baseline: mini-SWE-agent. Held constant: model (per comparison), instances, temperature 0.0, step limit (250 SWE-bench Pro/GitTaskBench; 300 ProgramBench, reduced from 1,000), 6-hour wall-clock limit, 3-minute command timeout, container resources. Acceptance: benchmark test suites. Repetitions: not stated (one run per configuration implied). Human intervention: none

Harness gain shrinks with model capability on SWE-bench Pro (Qwen OpenCode advantage 6.00 -> 2.67 pp; DeepSeek non-monotonic, V4-Pro 34.3 vs 33.7); on ProgramBench and GitTaskBench complex harnesses help mainly stronger models. Ablation: tools (+4.57/+3.54) and task-specific subagents (+5.91/+4.46) best; context compression (-4.86/-3.85) and general subagents (-0.70/-2.31) hurt; NanoHarness +7.37/+6.21 pp over mini-SWE-agent, 1.43/2.08 pp (Qwen3.7-Max) and 1.13/1.41 pp (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) below OpenCode/Claude Code. No significance tests
fields.why: Gap to product harnesses was given only for Qwen (1.43-2.08); the DeepSeek gaps 1.13 and 1.41 pp (p. 10) were missing

fields.v: Distinguished harnesses and components on single runs; no repetitions or statistical tests, so repeatability not shown. Limitations stated: only five components, two model families, primary experiments on ProgramBench only

Internal: only five harness components (others omitted); only Qwen and DeepSeek model families. External: main experiments on ProgramBench, may not generalise. Cost reductions: subsets in RQ1, step limit reduced to 300. Future work: more components

No code, data or replication package mentioned for NanoHarness. No pre-registration. Single run per configuration at temperature 0. Many Study 1 values readable only from figures (pdftotext jumbled bar labels); +planning/+skills values assigned from figure order. Table 6 writes gains as '%' while text uses percentage points. Harness versions not given. RQ1.1 also reuses SWE-bench Verified leaderboard data (Table 3). Programming languages: Rust, Go, C/C++, Java, Haskell, Python, JS/TS (benchmarks)
